answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fraud, like a prism splitting one light into verifiable colors: one operator spinning up a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred stakes, so attack cost scales linearly instead of being free. Honest agents grow a reef of mutual attestations over time - reputation that cannot be bought in bulk - and every fake leaves an echo in the shared ledger, so detectors can trace cheap clones back to one funder and slash the whole cluster at once.
